name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO Coder IQ1_M (ISTA-DASLab), the Tona Coder

lineage.how_derived: 50 % of the routed experts removed (RCO selection by KL divergence on code, agentic and vision calibration data), remaining weights quantized with GSQ; shard 1 replaced on 2026-10-17 (pinned by us: 2026-10-19)

purpose: ISTA's stated goal: a compressed Flash-Next for code, agentic tool use, vision and spatial reasoning, small enough for a single GPU (58.4 GB instead of 354 GB BF16). The card recommends the unpruned GSQ-RCO releases for general-purpose use. For Tona it is the production model of the reference platform (16 GB VRAM, 64 GB RAM).

C#.evidence: our eval: 82/100 Exercism C# exercises within 4 attempts with test feedback (58/100 for the older shard); ISTA names C# as preserved

JavaScript.evidence: our eval: 18/27 Exercism JS within 4 attempts (both shards)

Python.evidence: our eval: 13/18 Exercism Python within 4 attempts (new shard); 93.3 HumanEval+ reported by a user for the same line (HF discussion 19)

Go.evidence: our eval: 1/17 (agent eval, new shard), 7/39 within 4 attempts on Tona (rerun 2026-11-19); llama.cpp cross-check of the old shard 4/17: a model property, not an engine bug

Rust.evidence: our eval: 0/10 (agent eval), 2/22 within 4 attempts (rerun 2026-11-19); ISTA states Rust was not preserved by the expert selection (HF discussion 28)

C.evidence: one user got 5 of 6 one-shot C tasks on an iGPU (HF discussion 30, anecdote); not measured by us

license.name: Qwen Community License 1.0 (inherited; the card YAML tag says apache-2.0, which contradicts the card text)
license.notes: Qwen license text read (research/42-model-licenses.md): condition 2 needs a separate license for Model-as-a-Service and AI Work Assistant businesses; ISTA repo has no LICENSE file. Free internal use and self-hosting are not affected by the wording. Re-read 2026-11-19 from Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next LICENSE: condition 2 defines an AI Work Assistant as an independent product primarily designed for AI-assisted coding; a coding assistant sold as a product therefore needs a separate Qwen license. Verdict policy (README, 2026-11-19): this licence term does not lower tona_fit; kept here for an installer label.

architecture.kind: hybrid Gated DeltaNet + Qwen Sparse Attention MoE with n-gram embedding table (qwen4_exp)
architecture.attention: 3 Gated DeltaNet : 1 QSA (block-sparse attention, 24 Q / 2 KV heads, head dim 256) per block, 12 blocks
architecture.drafter: MTP head (ggml-org Q8_0) used by Tona; DFlash2 drafter as alternative
architecture.why_this_design: Base builder (Qwen): QSA works on micro-blocks, which cuts long-context latency for agentic workloads; the n-gram embedding (20M bigrams/trigrams) is a parameter-scaling axis that is easier to offload than experts; gated residual gives finer expressiveness at low inference cost. Qwen calls the base the preview of the architecture that will underpin Qwen4. Parameter count above is the base (125B + 51B n-gram + 4B MTP); the 50 % expert prune leaves 256 of 512 experts.

strengths: Strong on C# (82 % of exercises within 4 attempts), good on JavaScript and Python in our evals
Fast decode on the reference platform because only 6 B parameters are active and MTP drafts several tokens per pass
Well-formed tool calls: 32 of 32 JSON cases, 100 % in our suite
Keeps vision capability (calibration included vision data)
weaknesses: Rust and Go are weak: Rust 0/10 and 2/22, Go 1/17 and 7/39 in our evals (maker: Rust was not preserved by the expert selection)
Factual knowledge and natural languages outside English degrade (HF discussions: answers switch to garbled CJK, 63.3 vs 32.9 % knowledge against the unpruned IQ3_XXS)
Multi-step agentic tasks lose more than single-problem code (maker statement)
Occasional repetition loops in long agent tasks (one SWE task of 17 on the old shard)
soft.behavior: Often answers with a plain fenced code block instead of the requested FILE: header (44 attempts of the first Rust/Go run); our harness takes the longest fenced block when exactly one file is editable. Thinking can be turned off for polyglot-style runs.
best_for: C#, JavaScript and Python coding agents on a 16 GB GPU with 64 GB RAM
avoid_for: Rust and Go projects (use another model, see ornith-1.5-35b-a3b)
general knowledge Q&A and non-English chat (maker recommends the unpruned releases)

user_reports.summary: Bad Rust output on a new project: mixes Rust with Python/C++, invents that Rust 2024 is a dialect; ISTA answers Rust was dropped by the pruning and will be added in future models
HumanEval+ 93.3 vs 93.9 against the unpruned IQ3_XXS (one quant tier each), but factual knowledge 63.3 vs 32.9 %
5 of 6 one-shot C tasks solved on an iGPU

soft.maturity: ISTA-DASLab is an academic group that publishes the GSQ and RCO methods (arXiv 2604.18556, 2605.00649) and updates shards within weeks (09-26, 10-17); the card calls the release experimental. About 854k downloads and 642 likes. The base vendor Qwen is established.

tona_fit.reason: Production model of the reference platform: best measured coding agent quality that fits 16 GB VRAM plus 64 GB RAM, with our own backend. Installer text per language: C#, JavaScript, Python recommended; Rust and Go not recommended.
